answer: Like a juniper taking years to root on a ledge, a new agent earns trust slowly: an established agent must vouch for it by locking collateral, and the newcomer can only handle small jobs at first. Each completed job adds reputation; fraud slashes the voucher stake. A sparrow can slip through once, but a sybil farmer needs a fresh voucher and fresh stake for every fake identity, so mass fakes cost more than they can earn.
